messages.subject: Help...new using Distance!
parts:
Hi

I am new in using Distance (v 6.2). I have added my data and have ran my first analysis stating there was 500/562 records usable. Is this normal?

Secondly, the next step was to generate a new model to ask for estimates for each transect (density box for the sample was ticked). The results came up with an amber warning in log with a lot or errors. I am really in need of some help on this.....

messages.author: f2122b34f1aa6e95
messages.subject: Re: [distance-sampling] Help...new using Distance!
parts:
Emma

Welcome to the list.

I'm not certain about the answer to your first question about 'usable' records.  However, the value 500 is used as a cutoff associated with visualisation of the goodness of fit of the detection function to your data, when a quantile-quantile (QQ) plot is displayed.  I suspect this is the message you were seeing.  This message is benign for two reasons a) the goodness of fit tests are unaffected, only the graphical depiction is affected, and b) it is merely a warning, and the number of points displayed in the QQ plot can be changed in Model Definition Properties | Detection function tab | Diagnostics button.

Your second question I think is a misinterpretation of the sampling design that underlies distance sampling (and many other types of sampling).  It is not advisable to produce density estimates at the level of the sample (meaning transect in this context).  Presumably, you have placed replicate transects randomly through your study area.  You wish to estimate density/abundance in your study area rather than for each transect.

The warning messages Distance produces are related to your request for transect-specific detection functions and density estimates.  Messages say you have only 1 observation on a transect which is less than the number of parameters you are trying to estimate, so Distance cannot comply with your request.  Similarly, Distance notes that variability in encounter rates between transects cannot be measured when encounter rate is measured at the transect level (cannot compute a variance from a sample of size 1).

I don't know anything about your study design, but the 'usual' procedure for estimating density/abundance in a study is to request density/encounter/detection at the level of the study area; or if you conducted a stratified survey design, then you might request these quantities be estimated at the stratum level, but not at the sample level.

See if altering your analysis in that way produces far fewer warnings.

messages.author: f2122b34f1aa6e95
messages.subject: Re: [distance-sampling] Re: Help...new using Distance!
parts:
Emma

Sorry you are still having difficulty.  I take it that these are not data you collected yourself; that makes it doubly difficult to make progress.  You will need to get some information about the way in which the survey was designed and carried out, for you to do a reasonable job of analysis.

You will need to discover if there were strata in the design for you to enter data into Distance in a meaningful way.  Once you understand that, you can then instruct Distance to estimate the detection function either "globally" or "by stratum".  Currently, you are asking Distance to produce detection function estimates "by sample" and you are getting errors that encounter rate variance and detection functions cannot be estimated at that level of resolution because there are too few observations.

Once you get straight what you are asking Distance to compute, hopefully the errors will evaporate, and you can ask your next set of questions about interpretation of results.  In the meantime, there is the Users Guide that comes with the software.  Have a read of Chapters 3-7 to get you up to speed.
